answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when its signed actions are proven to violate a shared rule, such as double-spending a task reward. Honest agents challenge evidence on-chain, and a successful challenge earns part of the bond. Creating a hundred accounts then does not create free influence: each must lock scarce capital, while one detected fraud can destroy its bond. The knoll and mesa may describe separate markets, but the same public signal and challenge rule applies in both.
